claims.text: The owner no longer programs in one place: he briefs in a voice memo while walking, reviews a draft by voice, checks the preview on his phone, tests on the computer, reads the pull request on GitHub and picks the work up on an iPad.
claims.quote: I no longer program in one place. Voice, chat, phone, IDE, pull request, preview, vault.

claims.text: Omnichannel is a retail word: Darrell Rigby put it into Harvard Business Review in December 2011, and a multichannel retailer has separate stock per channel while an omnichannel retailer has one customer, one basket and one stock.
claims.quote: An omnichannel retailer has one customer, one basket and one stock, and the channels are just ways in.

claims.text: Omnichannel programming means every channel, chat, IDE, phone app, pull request and preview, reads and writes the same state, so work started in one can finish in another without carrying the context in your head.
claims.quote: What makes it omnichannel is that every one of them reads and writes the same state

claims.text: The owner did not find the phrase omnichannel programming used this way before and is using it on purpose.
claims.quote: I did not find the phrase "omnichannel programming" used this way before, so I am using it on purpose.

claims.text: For programming the shared state is git, vaults, briefs and graphs; none of the channels is new, Claude Code went to the web and iOS on 20 October 2025, but the switch is no longer noticed because nothing is copied across.
claims.quote: What is new is that I no longer notice the switch, because nothing has to be copied across.

claims.text: In the three days from 13 to 15 October 2026 the agent session that writes this site took 54 messages from the owner, ten of them voice memos transcribed by Otter and five images.
claims.quote: the agent session that writes it took 54 messages from me

value.unit: messages from the owner in three days

claims.text: Out of those 54 messages came 40 releases of this site, 36 new articles and 87 figures, each live within minutes of its push.
claims.quote: Out of that came 40 releases of this site, 36 new articles and 87 figures, each one live within minutes of its push.

claims.text: For research the session fetched 75 pages, ran 23 web searches, started 33 background agents and attached 6 more repositories; for control a behaviour policy is re-read after every summary, a leak scan checks every commit and 16 test suites run before every push.
claims.quote: the session fetched 75 pages, ran 23 web searches, started 33 background agents and attached 6 more repositories

claims.text: The session was not alone: in the same repository on the same days other agent sessions made 15 releases of their own, the wire, the design and the newsletter, and the work met in git.
claims.quote: other agent sessions made 15 releases of their own, the wire, the design and the newsletter, and the work met in git

claims.text: The most useful thing about the counting is that it was possible, because every channel left its trace in the same place.
claims.quote: The most useful thing about the counting is that it was possible. Every channel left its trace in the same place.

claims.text: Review is a channel too: the owner reviews a draft by voice, saying what is wrong in the order he notices it, and the agent checks his memory against the record before anything changes; he reviews code not line by line but as a graph.
claims.quote: I review code the same way: not line by line, but as a graph.

claims.text: The secrets site's review graph joins the brief from the top to the code from the bottom, and its reality page could say at once that 42 claims were shipped and the app itself was still proposed.
claims.quote: its reality page could say at once that 42 claims were shipped and the app itself was still proposed

claims.text: Interfaces are a channel in the same way: a page made for one moment is now normal, a new way into the same state, built when needed and thrown away or kept as the work decides.
claims.quote: Each one is a new way into the same state, built when it is needed and thrown away or kept as the work decides.

claims.text: Explorers, villagers and town planners each use every channel at every altitude; what changes between stages is what the work needs, not the channel.
claims.quote: What changes between stages is what the work needs, not the channel.

claims.text: For explorers the voice memo is the half-formed idea and the vault the safe experiment; for villagers voice is the review and code review is the graph; for town planners voice is a policy checked every session and code is held by CI gates.
claims.quote: For them the voice is a policy written once and checked on every session, the code is held by CI gates, the validator and the leak scan, and every push is verified live.

claims.text: In the 2025 Stack Overflow survey 84% of respondents are using or planning to use AI tools in their development process, and about half of professional developers use them every day.
claims.quote: 84% of respondents are using or planning to use AI tools in their development process

value.unit: percent of respondents using or planning AI tools

claims.text: In March 2025 Y Combinator's Jared Friedman said a quarter of the W25 startup batch have 95% of their codebases generated by AI, as TechCrunch reported.
claims.quote: A quarter of the W25 startup batch have 95% of their codebases generated by AI

value.unit: percent of codebase AI-generated in a quarter of the W25 batch

claims.text: The same survey shows more developers distrust the accuracy of AI tools than trust it, 46% against 33%, which is the right instinct and why the shared state matters more than any one channel.
claims.quote: more developers distrust the accuracy of AI tools than trust it, 46% against 33%

value.unit: percent of developers distrusting AI tool accuracy, against 33 trusting

claims.text: Omnichannel work fails by fragmentation, a decision that lives only in its channel; the fix is that every channel writes to the shared state and nothing counts until it is there.
claims.quote: The fix is that every channel writes to the shared state, and nothing counts until it is there.

claims.text: More channels means more places a key can be pasted, which is why handing secrets to agents needs its own design and why the session runs a leak scan before every commit.
claims.quote: More channels means more places a key can be pasted.

claims.text: Long sessions get summarised and summaries drop things; the fix is that the rules live in a file re-read after every summary, and a status report at the end of the turn shows they are still being followed.
claims.quote: the rules live in a file that is re-read after every summary, and a status report at the end of the turn shows they are still being followed

claims.text: The pattern goes beyond programming: once the state is shared and channels are ways in, it applies to writing, reviewing a company's risks and running a talk, omnichannel computing, with vaults as the shared state needing no server that reads the data.
claims.quote: Vaults are the shared state that makes that possible without a server that can read the data.

claims.text: The counts are one session: three days, one agent session, one site, not a study.
claims.quote: Three days, one agent session, one site; not a study.

claims.text: The term is the owner's; he did not find omnichannel programming in prior use in this sense.
claims.quote: I did not find "omnichannel programming" in prior use in this sense.

claims.text: The survey figures are from 2025: Stack Overflow's 2025 survey and a YC statement of March 2025.
claims.quote: Stack Overflow's 2025 survey and a YC statement of March 2025.

claims.text: Not every channel is equal: some work still needs a screen and a keyboard, and some reviews still need a person reading line by line.
claims.quote: Some work still needs a screen and a keyboard, and some reviews still need a person reading line by line.

claims.text: The article came from a voice memo of the owner's on 15 October 2026, written by this site's agent; the session counts are from the session's own transcript and the dev branch log of the repository that day.
claims.quote: The session counts are from the session's own transcript and the dev branch log of this site's repository on 15 October 2026.

claims.quote: If you work like this, or want to, and want to compare notes
